facts.raw_span: progressive unilateral skin hardening on his right thigh and buttock for 7 years
motion of his right limb joint was slightly limited
ill-defined, stony-hard plaque involving his right thigh above the patella extending to his right buttocks with loss of skin elasticity
mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation
Normal results for routine blood tests
Normal results for autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality on MRI of right thigh
Normal epidermis and mild pigmentation along the basal layer with subtle increase in density of fibroblasts extending to the subcutis and forming adipocyte entrapment but no evidence of inflammation
Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Negative Alcian blue staining
Dense reticular dermis extended below well-preserved appendages
no evidence of inflammation

concepts.why: The patient's progressive unilateral skin hardening, ill-defined plaque, and increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis are consistent with scleroderma.
The patient's skin hardening, plaque, and hypertrichosis are consistent with morphea, a form of localized scleroderma.
The patient's skin hardening, plaque, and subcutaneous tissue thickening are consistent with lipodermatosclerosis.
The patient's skin hardening, plaque, and increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis are consistent with eosinophilic fasciitis.
The patient's skin hardening, plaque, and subcutaneous tissue thickening are consistent with nephrogenic systemic fibrosis.
The patient's skin hardening, plaque, and hypertrichosis are consistent with panniculitis.
The patient's skin hardening, plaque, and subcutaneous tissue thickening are consistent with scleredema.
The patient's skin hardening, plaque, and increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis are consistent with fibrosing dermopathy.
It explains the histopathological finding of increased density of fibroblasts extending to the subcutis and forming adipocyte entrapment without evidence of inflammation.

rationales.F09: Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis can be seen in morphea and other fibrosing conditions.
rationales.F11: Dense reticular dermis extending below well-preserved appendages is characteristic of morphea and some other fibrosing disorders.
